title: What Personal Flight Vehicles Is
definition: Personal Flight Vehicles: safe personal aircraft for everyday use.
description:
Personal Flight Vehicles: safe personal aircraft for everyday use. This is Future Transport & Mobility at its most ambitious — lift fans research, vehicle logistics engineering and autonomy stacks operations converging on a single goal: making vehicle hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Transport & Mobility will decide vertiports outcomes this century. Personal Flight Vehicles is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working vehicle hulls, the larger lift fans vision stalls, and with it, the vehicle logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Personal Flight Vehicles in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Personal Flight Vehicles
title: Real Research Today: Personal Flight Vehicles
definition: Today's documented research behind Personal Flight Vehicles.
description:
The road to Personal Flight Vehicles is already being paved. NASA's X-59 QueSST and Boom Supersonic's XB-1 pursue quiet supersonic flight. The eVTOL industry (Joby, Archer, Lilium) certifies electric air taxis with aviation authorities.

Autonomous shipping trials (Yara Birkeland, MAS) test crewless cargo vessels. Together these programs form the lift fans foundation that Personal Flight Vehicles will build on — the vehicle logistics results, the autonomy stacks methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as vehicle logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Personal Flight Vehicles
definition: Estimates Personal Flight Vehicles readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Personal Flight Vehicles components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a vehicle hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Personal Flight Vehicles Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Personal Flight Vehicles operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Personal Flight Vehicles installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 19282 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where lift fans monitoring, vehicle logistics redundancy, or autonomy stacks maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Personal Flight Vehicles Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Personal Flight Vehicles: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Personal Flight Vehicles — safe personal aircraft for everyday use.

Phase 1 — Prove (lift fans): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (vehicle logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (autonomy stacks): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (vertiports): vehicle hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and consumers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
